q: The magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic ____ through that loop.
e: The magnitude of induced emf in a wire loop is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux through that loop. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: For a wire loop with N identical turns, $E = $ ____.
e: For a wire loop with N identical turns, E = -N (dPhiB)/(dt). The relation in this line is E = ____. A nearby word in place of -N (dPhiB)/(dt) would name a different quantity.

q: If the wire loop is not moving (or) is moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is no induced emf (or) induced ____.
e: If the wire loop is not moving (or) is moving parallel to the magnetic field lines, there is no induced emf (or) induced current. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

q: Faraday's law gives the magnitude of the induced emf and ____ law gives its direction.
e: Faraday's law gives the magnitude of the induced emf and Lenz's law gives its direction. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. Faraday's law: induced emf equals the rate of change of magnetic flux through the loop.

q: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic ____ that causes it.
e: An induced emf is always in a direction that opposes the change in the original magnetic flux that causes it. Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current.

q: The direction of induced current can be found by applying ____ law.
e: The direction of induced current can be found by applying Lenz's law. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it.

q: The change in magnetic flux is, in fact, a decrease or an increase in the magnetic lines of ____.
e: The change in magnetic flux is, in fact, a decrease or an increase in the magnetic lines of force. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. A decrease or an increase in the magnetic lines of ____. force.

q: Lenz's law is a good example of the principle of conservation of ____.
e: Lenz's law is a good example of the principle of conservation of energy. Lenz's law sets the sign: the induced emf fights the flux change that made it. Lenz is the name attached to this result.

q: It shows how the energy from the mechanical work done against the opposing force experienced by the moving magnet or rotating coil is transformed into ____ energy.
e: It shows how the energy from the mechanical work done against the opposing force experienced by the moving magnet or rotating coil is transformed into electrical energy. The moving magnet or rotating coil is transformed into ____ energy. electrical. A nearby word in place of electrical would name a different quantity.

q: When a magnet is moved towards the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil ____.
e: When a magnet is moved towards the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil increases. Flux is B A cosθ; full when B is perpendicular to the area and zero when B lies in the plane. Moved towards the coil, the magnetic flux through the coil ____. increases.

q: The induced current in the coil must produce a magnetic field which opposes an ____ in the original magnetic flux.
e: The induced current in the coil must produce a magnetic field which opposes an increase in the original magnetic flux. A changing magnetic flux through a loop produces an induced emf and, if the path is closed, an induced current. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.

q: Therefore, the current in the coil must be flowing in a counter clockwise direction if viewed from the magnet according to right-hand ____.
e: Therefore, the current in the coil must be flowing in a counter clockwise direction if viewed from the magnet according to right-hand rule. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. Clockwise direction if viewed from the magnet according to right-hand ____. rule.
